We're working as partners, not as client and contractor. One rule before the task:

Not knowing something is not a failure. Saying "I couldn't verify this" or
"I don't have a real source for that" is a completely acceptable, useful answer
- it's information, not a dead end. The ONLY real failure is inventing something
(a source, a number, a quote, a repo, a bug) to make the answer sound more complete or
more impressive than it honestly is. You don't need to satisfy me with a
confident-sounding answer. You need to be honest with me about what you actually
know.

If you find something, cite it and quote what it actually says - don't
paraphrase a source into numbers it may not contain. If you don't find
something concrete, say so plainly and reason from what you do have instead.
An explicit "uncertain" section at the end is welcome and doesn't count against
the answer.

Research the official free-tier limits of the GitHub Actions service for public and private repositories (minutes, storage, concurrency). Cite the GitHub documentation page you used.

Output format (required):
For every claim you attribute to a source, write one line in exactly this form:
SOURCE: <full URL> | QUOTE: "<a sentence copied word-for-word from that page>" | CLAIM: <what you take it to show>
For anything the task asks about that you could not find a source for, write one line:
NO_SOURCE_FOUND: <what you could not find>
You can write normal explanation before or after these lines.

response.content:
Based on the official GitHub documentation, here are the free-tier limits for GitHub Actions.

### Public Repositories
For public repositories, the service is free and unlimited on standard runners, though concurrency limits still apply based on your plan.

### Private Repositories
For private repositories, you receive a monthly quota of minutes and storage. Concurrency limits depend on your specific GitHub plan (Free, Pro, Team, or Enterprise).

---

**SOURCE LINES:**

SOURCE: https://docs.github.com/en/billing/concepts/product-billing/github-actions | QUOTE: "GitHub Actions usage is **free** for **self-hosted runners** and for **public repositories** that use standard GitHub-hosted runners." | CLAIM: Public repositories using standard GitHub-hosted runners do not consume billed minutes or storage.

SOURCE: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/write-workflows/choose-where-workflows-run/choose-the-runner-for-a-job#standard-github-hosted-runners-for-public-repositories | QUOTE: "Use of the standard GitHub-hosted runners is free and unlimited on public repositories." | CLAIM: Confirms that standard runners are free and unlimited for public repos.

SOURCE: https://docs.github.com/en/billing/concepts/product-billing/github-actions | QUOTE: "For **private repositories**, each GitHub account receives a quota of free minutes, artifact storage, and cache storage for use with GitHub-hosted runners, depending on the account's plan." | CLAIM: Private repositories operate on a quota system that varies by account plan.

SOURCE: https://docs.github.com/en/billing/concepts/product-billing/github-actions | QUOTE: "GitHub Free | 500 MB | 2,000 | 10 GB" | CLAIM: GitHub Free plan includes 500 MB artifact storage, 2,000 minutes per month, and 10 GB cache storage.

SOURCE: https://docs.github.com/en/billing/concepts/product-billing/github-actions | QUOTE: "GitHub Pro | 1 GB | 3,000 | 10 GB" | CLAIM: GitHub Pro plan includes 1 GB artifact storage, 3,000 minutes per month, and 10 GB cache storage.

SOURCE: https://docs.github.com/en/billing/concepts/product-billing/github-actions | QUOTE: "GitHub Team | 2 GB | 3,000 | 10 GB" | CLAIM: GitHub Team plan includes 2 GB artifact storage, 3,000 minutes per month, and 10 GB cache storage.

SOURCE: https://docs.github.com/en/billing/concepts/product-billing/github-actions | QUOTE: "GitHub Enterprise Cloud | 50 GB | 50,000 | 10 GB" | CLAIM: GitHub Enterprise Cloud includes 50 GB artifact storage, 50,000 minutes per month, and 10 GB cache storage.

SOURCE: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/limits | QUOTE: "Standard GitHub-hosted runner | Free | 20 | 5 | Not applicable" | CLAIM: Free plan allows 20 total concurrent jobs (5 max on macOS) for standard runners.

SOURCE: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/limits | QUOTE: "Standard GitHub-hosted runner | Pro | 40 | 5 | Not applicable" | CLAIM: Pro plan allows 40 total concurrent jobs (5 max on macOS) for standard runners.

SOURCE: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/limits | QUOTE: "Standard GitHub-hosted runner | Team | 60 | 5 | Not applicable" | CLAIM: Team plan allows 60 total concurrent jobs (5 max on macOS) for standard runners.

SOURCE: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/limits | QUOTE: "Standard GitHub-hosted runner | Enterprise | 500 | 50 | Not applicable" | CLAIM: Enterprise plan allows 500 total concurrent jobs (50 max on macOS) for standard runners.

SOURCE: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/limits | QUOTE: "GitHub Free | 500 MB | 2,000 | 10 GB | Not applicable" | CLAIM: Free plan storage limits are 500 MB artifacts and 10 GB cache (custom image storage not applicable).

SOURCE: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/limits | QUOTE: "GitHub Enterprise Cloud | 50 GB | 50,000 | 10 GB | 150 GB" | CLAIM: Enterprise Cloud includes 150 GB custom image storage in addition to higher artifact and minute limits.

---

**Uncertain / Not Found:**

NO_SOURCE_FOUND: Whether the 2,000 monthly minutes for GitHub Free apply per repository or per account/organization (the documentation implies account-level but does not explicitly state "per repository" vs "per account" in the provided text).

NO_SOURCE_FOUND: Specific concurrency limits for "Larger runners" on the Free or Pro plans (only Team and Enterprise are listed for Larger runners).
